subject: english-language
title: Talk at Work
welcome_lead: Every profession has its dialect of expertise. Tour the workplace and listen to the rhythms of institutional talk.
meta_desc: Drew & Heritage's institutional talk and workplace discourse at A-Level English Language.
final_note: You have mapped the dialect of the workplace — goal-driven, asymmetric and densely coded.

concepts.def: Drew & Heritage (1992) — workplace interactions characterised by goal-orientation, asymmetry and special inferential frameworks.
Workplace talk is organised around institutional purposes (treatment, transaction, instruction).
One participant typically controls topic, turns and evaluation (doctor vs patient, manager vs subordinate).
Specialist vocabulary shared by an occupational group; can index expertise but also exclude outsiders.
Talk between specialists and non-specialists, requiring accommodation and translation of jargon.
Speakers performing professional roles through register, lexis and discourse strategies.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Drew and Heritage (1992) identified three core features of institutional talk: goal-orientation, special constraints on contributions, and distinctive inferential frameworks.

A 999 call is not just a chat — its structure is geared toward extracting actionable information fast.

Jargon does double duty. To insiders it is efficient — a single term replaces a paragraph. To outsiders it can be alienating, gatekeeping access.

Workplace texts often code-switch: jargon among colleagues, simplified explanation for clients.

Doctor-patient consultations show accommodation in action. Doctors deploy hedges, analogies and lay synonyms to bridge knowledge asymmetry.

Effective expert-lay communication is a skill — and a research field.

mcqs.q: Are features of spoken language like 'um' and 'you know' signs of poor speech?
options: No — they are functional discourse markers and planning devices that help interaction flow, manage turn-taking and signal speaker meaning.
Fillers and false starts show the speaker is uneducated.
Spoken language has no rules unlike written language.

mcqs.q: What did Chomsky propose about language acquisition?
options: Chomsky said children should be taught grammar from age two.
Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Children possess an innate Language Acquisition Device — an inborn capacity for grammar — because exposure alone cannot account for how rapidly and uniformly children learn complex syntax.
Chomsky said children learn language entirely by copying adults.

mcqs.q: What is Skinner's behaviourist view of language acquisition?
options: Skinner believed children couldn't learn language until age five.
Children learn language through imitation and operant conditioning — they are reinforced for correct utterances and corrected for errors.
Skinner believed in an innate grammar module.
Spoken language has no rules unlike written language.
